answers.text: I have nine years in consulting, the last five as an engagement manager at a global firm. I lead teams of four to six consultants on 9 to 12-week engagements, and I have delivered 11 of them. The one I'm proudest of was a cost-reduction programme for a manufacturing client, where we identified savings of about 14% of addressable spend. I'm applying now because I advise on decisions that someone else carries out, and I want to be the person who carries them out.
I can't name the client or share the rupee value of the savings. Our engagement letters prohibit that. The 14% figure is already the most I can say about it.
My leadership style is collaborative and empowering. I focus on creating a high-performance culture and aligning the team towards a common vision, while ensuring client delight.
On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead. A partner designed the whole approach and I only built the spreadsheets.
I'm not sure it is fair to say a consultant has no accountability for results. We are measured on whether the client implements our recommendations. I would rather you ask how I follow through.
